facts.claim: 澤西機場10月31日晚間再度因機場附近出現無人機而受擾，4架班機未能按計畫降落。
10月31日受影響班機包括由馬德拉飛來的包機轉降巴黎戴高樂機場，倫敦蓋特威克與希斯洛班機嚴重延誤，洛根航空晚間8時30分由南安普敦出發的班機取消。
澤西機場稱擾動源於機場周邊非法且持續的無人機活動，航空公司正直接為受影響旅客安排替代行程。
前一晚10月30日亦有3架進場班機因無人機通報而轉降，警方約晚間8時20分接獲首宗通報，通報持續至約晚間10時30分。
澤西首席部長林登法納姆稱連續兩晚的事件蓄意且違法，政府正與英國當局及專業機構合作研議額外營運支援、偵測能力與反無人機技術。

zh.title: 澤西機場連續第二晚受無人機擾動，4架班機未能按計畫降落

en.title: Jersey Airport (JER) hit by drone disruption for second consecutive night, four flights unable to land as scheduled
en.summary: Jersey Airport suffered a second evening of disruption on October 31 after further drone activity near the airfield, with four flights unable to land as scheduled; the previous evening three inbound aircraft were diverted, and Jersey's chief minister described the two evenings' incidents as deliberate and unlawful.
body: Jersey Airport (JER) experienced a second evening of disruption on Saturday, October 31, after further drone activity was reported near the airfield, with four flights unable to land as scheduled, according to the airport. An inbound charter flight from Madeira was diverted to Paris Charles de Gaulle, flights from London Gatwick and London Heathrow (LHR) faced lengthy delays, and Loganair's 8:30 p.m. service from Southampton was cancelled.

In a statement on Saturday evening, Jersey Airport said the disruption had been caused by what it described as illegal and persistent drone activity around the airport, and that airlines were arranging alternative travel plans directly with affected passengers. The disruption came one day after three inbound aircraft were diverted on Friday, October 30, following reports of drones near the airport, with police receiving the first report at around 8:20 p.m. UTC and further reports continuing until about 10:30 p.m. UTC. Jersey Chief Minister Senator Lyndon Farnham described the incidents over the two evenings as deliberate and unlawful, and said the government was working with UK authorities and specialist agencies to explore additional operational support, improved detection capabilities, and counter-drone technology; no drone operators had been identified at the time of the police update.
